About AURA:

We are developing AURA (Autonomous Unified Remote Assessment) for NASA Space Apps—an autonomous system monitoring health metrics and environmental safety for astronauts.

Looking for teammates skilled in:

• Embedded Systems & Electronics (Microcontrollers, Sensors)

• Software & UI/UX (Dashboards)

• Data Analysis & AI (Telemetry)

• Pitching & Documentation
summary:
AURA-Space is a mobile application designed to help astronauts monitor and assess their health during space missions.

The application allows astronauts to manually enter health data, such as heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, sleep duration, and mental well-being, as well as record any symptoms they experience.

It focuses on four main health areas: cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, immune, and mental and behavioral health.

The system relies on a personal medical profile for each astronaut, containing their medical history and baseline health information. We also studied medical information from NASA reports and scientific papers, with the aim of organizing it into a medical database for future AI model training. However, due to the limited time during the challenge, we could not complete the data organization.

The application is designed to analyze health data in relation to the astronaut's medical profile, identify potential health risks and conditions, and suggest relevant examinations and medical guidance.

It also supports offline operation, helping astronauts monitor their health and identify potential problems early, especially when communication with Earth is limited.
details:
AURA-Space – Project Details

1. Project Functionality & How It Works

AURA-Space is a mobile application we developed to help astronauts monitor and assess their health during space missions.

The application allows astronauts to manually enter their health data, such as heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, sleep duration, and mental well-being. They can also report any symptoms they experience.

The application focuses on four main health areas:

  • Cardiovascular Health.
  • Musculoskeletal Health.
  • Immune System.
  • Mental and Behavioral Health.

Each astronaut has a personal medical profile containing their medical history and baseline health information. The application is designed to use this profile along with newly entered data to assess their health and identify unusual changes.

How Does It Work?

The application follows several steps, starting with creating the astronaut's medical profile and ending with displaying the health assessment results.

First: Account & Medical Profile

Before the mission, the astronaut creates an account and enters their medical information, including:

  • Medical History.
  • Previous Medical Conditions.
  • Allergies.
  • Current Medications.
  • Baseline Health Data.

This information is stored in the astronaut's personal medical profile and used as a reference during the mission.

Second: Health Data Input

During the mission, the astronaut manually enters their health data, including:

  • Heart Rate.
  • Blood Pressure.
  • Blood Glucose.
  • Body Temperature.
  • Sleep Duration.
  • Mood.
  • Symptoms.

Third: Data Processing & Analysis

The application is designed to compare newly entered health data with the information in the astronaut's medical profile and use relevant medical knowledge from NASA research and scientific references.

This process aims to identify unusual changes, analyze reported symptoms, relate them to relevant medical information, and identify possible health risks and conditions, as well as examinations that may be needed.

Fourth: Health Assessment Results

After processing the data, the application is designed to display health assessment results, including:

  • Health Status: An overview of the astronaut's current health condition.
  • Possible Conditions: Potential health conditions related to the available data.
  • Risk Level: An indication of the potential health risk.
  • Recommended Examinations: Medical examinations that may help evaluate the condition.
  • Medical Guidance: Relevant guidance and recommendations.

Fifth: Medical Record Update

New health data and assessment results can be added to the astronaut's medical record, allowing health changes to be tracked and compared over time.

The application also supports offline operation, reducing the need for a continuous internet connection during space missions.

Overall, the proposed process follows this sequence:

Create Medical Profile → Enter Health Data → Process and Analyze Data → Assess Health → Display Results and Recommendations → Update Medical Record.

2. Benefits

AURA-Space aims to provide several benefits, including:

  • Providing an organized way for astronauts to monitor their health.
  • Helping identify unusual health changes and indicators.
  • Considering each astronaut's medical history and baseline health data during assessment.
  • Supporting the identification of potential health risks and conditions.
  • Providing suggested medical examinations and relevant guidance.
  • Making essential health information available without requiring a continuous internet connection.
  • Maintaining health records to track changes over time.

3. Expected Impact

Our goal is to improve how astronauts monitor their health and help them understand changes that may occur due to exposure to the space environment.

We expect the application to support early identification of potential health risks, improve individual health monitoring, and provide information that can help astronauts make more informed health-related decisions, especially during long-duration missions where communication with Earth may be limited.

In the long term, AURA-Space could provide a foundation for developing more advanced health monitoring and assessment systems using artificial intelligence for space missions.

4. Tools & Technologies

We worked on several technical and research aspects to develop the project, including:

  • Mobile Application Development: Designing and developing a mobile application interface that allows astronauts to enter their health data and view health-related information.
  • NASA Research: Studying and reviewing medical information from NASA reports and scientific publications, especially those related to astronaut health and the Human Research Program (HRP).
  • Medical Information Review: Identifying relevant health conditions, symptoms, indicators, and medical information from the reviewed scientific resources.
  • Dataset Development (Future Work): Organizing the collected medical information into a structured dataset remains a planned development step.
  • Artificial Intelligence (Future Work): Developing and training an AI model specialized in analyzing and assessing astronauts' health using the planned medical dataset.

We reviewed and gathered relevant medical information from NASA reports and scientific research. However, due to the limited time available during the challenge, we could not complete organizing this information into a structured dataset or building and training the AI model. Both remain important parts of our future development plans.

5. Creative Aspect

The main creative idea behind AURA-Space is combining each astronaut's personal medical profile with medical knowledge related to human health in the space environment.

Instead of treating every health reading separately, the system aims to assess new data in the context of each astronaut's medical history and baseline health information.

The project also focuses on four main health areas while considering the risks associated with space conditions. In addition, it supports offline operation to address the communication limitations of space missions.

Another important aspect is the use of NASA research and scientific publications as a medical foundation for future development, including the planned creation of a specialized medical dataset and AI model.

6. Factors Considered During Development

During development, we considered several factors that affect astronauts' health and the way they use the application:

  • Space Environment: The effects of microgravity and space radiation on the human body.
  • Isolation and Confinement: The physical and psychological effects of isolation and staying for long periods in a confined environment.
  • Limited Communication: The possibility of delayed or interrupted communication with Earth, which is why we considered offline operation.
  • Individual Medical History: Differences in medical history, health conditions, and baseline health data between astronauts.
  • Medical Information Reliability: Referring to NASA research, reports, and scientific publications when studying health risks and medical conditions.
  • Early Risk Detection: Focusing on monitoring health indicators and unusual changes to help identify potential problems early.
  • Medical Safety: Designing the application as a health monitoring and decision-support tool, not as a replacement for doctors or professional medical care.

Conclusion

Our goal is to develop AURA-Space into a tool that helps astronauts monitor their health and understand changes in their bodies during space missions. It combines personal medical information with scientific research focused on spaceflight health risks. Future development will focus on organizing the reviewed medical information into a structured dataset and integrating a specialized AI model to enhance health assessment and decision support.
dataRefs: We used NASA's Human Research Roadmap to explore the health risks associated with spaceflight, understand their potential effects on astronauts, and identify the medical conditions relevant to our project.

We used NASA Human Research Program (HRP) evidence reports and scientific publications as our main sources of medical information.  These reports cover different health areas, including cardiovascular health, bone and muscle loss, immune system changes, radiation exposure, nutrition, sleep, behavioral health, medical conditions, and other spaceflight-related risks.  We reviewed these reports to extract relevant medical information, such as health conditions, causes, symptoms, indicators, detection methods, medical examinations, complications, and recommendations.  We then organized the extracted information into a structured JSON dataset to support the development of AURA-Space and serve as a foundation for future AI model training.
